text:
oncall-bot: :rotating_light: [ALERT] 5xx surge + p99 timeouts in us-west-2 for inference gateway - increase in gateway 502/504s and client timeouts. paging @sara @mike for primary oncall.

sara: seeing the alert dashboard. p95 ~ 900ms -> 1.8s, p99 pegged at 4.2s, errors ramping to ~12% 5xx across /v1/generate. Is this a deploy?

mike: I rolled a canary 12m ago (commit: f3d9a2) that touched egress proxy routing and keepalive defaults. Canary looked fine in staging. I'm checking deploy logs now.

linda: logs show a lot of upstream connection resets from gateway -> runtime. example: ```2026-02-19T22:10:11Z gateway=warn conn_reset upstream=10.0.45.12:443 id=xyz status=502```. Also seeing slow DNS lookups.

james: telemetry: KV cache utilization jumped during canary, and connection pool saturation increased by 3x for the egress pool. Might be connection churn.

infra-bot: Top traces: most 5xx originate from route /v1/generate -> egress-proxy -> runtime-pool. Errors grouped by backend host.

sara: ok, prioritize mitigation. Options: rollback canary, reduce canary traffic, open circuit on egress-proxy routing, bump connection pool size, or enable fallback model routing. Thoughts?

mike: quick check: can we flip canary traffic to 0%? I can cut it in the deploy system but want to know customer impact if we do immediate rollback.

cs-ops: customer-impact signals: increased error reports from a handful of large tenants using streaming. Estimated affected QPS ~1200 for the last 10 minutes, error budget burn high. Some real-time features degraded.

linda: reproduction curl from a control host: ```curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDACTED" https://gateway-us-west.redwood.ai/v1/generate -d '{"input":"hello"}'``` returns 502 after 1.2s consistently during the window.

sara: mike, if we rollback to previous revision quickly that's safest. Can you initiate rollback and coordinate with on-call deploy ops? We need to preserve canary artifacts for postmortem.

mike: initiating rollback now. ops-bot, please trigger immediate rollback of deploy f3d9a2 -> previous stable f2b7e1.

ops-bot: Rollback request received. Starting rollback to f2b7e1 across us-west-2. Estimated rollforward time 90s per shard, rolling across 6 shards. Posting updates as shards flip.

linda: while rollback in flight, can we temporarily increase connection pool size on gateway to mitigate sticky failures? might help if rollout is slower.

james: pool increase is a config flip that needs restart; it will be more disruptive than rollback. I'd prefer rollback first.

ops-bot: Shard 1 rollback complete. health checks passing.

ops-bot: Shard 2 rollback complete. Shard 3 in progress.

infra-bot: Metric check: error rate dropping on Shard 1 -> 4.6% down from 12%. p99 still high until shard 2 flips.

sara: good. keep canary traffic at 0 and do not re-deploy the canary until postmortem.

ops-bot: Shard 3 rollback complete. Shard 4,5,6 starting.

linda: after shard3 flip, I see 503->200 transition in logs for many hosts. Latency p95 back to 700ms on shard3.

mike: rollback complete across all shards. Final check in progress.

infra-bot: Post-rollback telemetry: global error rate down to 1.2%, p95 back to 650ms, p99 1.1s. Connection pool saturation returned to normal baselines.

sara: excellent. immediate mitigation successful. Next steps: create incident ticket, assign postmortem owners (mike + linda + james), and gather canary artifacts + trace spans.

cs-ops: Customer impact note: several customers reported degraded streaming experiences for ~15 minutes; we'll draft an outbound note to affected customers.

mike: quick hypothesis: canary changed egress proxy keepalive settings which increased connection churn under rolling traffic patterns; combined with DNS/ephemeral backend routing caused upstream resets. Need to reproduce locally and write integration test for connection stability.

linda: saving relevant logs/trace IDs: span ids: [span-6c7b, span-6c8d, span-6d1f] (saved to incident bucket).

james: I'll scrub metrics for any KV cache eviction spikes that align. If we can reproduce churn in loadgen with stable DNS we can validate.

sara: plan for postmortem: timeline, RCA, mitigation actions (blocklist canary until q/a signoff, integration tests, add e2e canary for keepalive), customer comms draft. Target: postmortem published within 72 hours.

ops-bot: Incident ticket created: INC-2026-0453. Assigning owners.

oncall-bot: If anything regresses, re-paging escalation to sevpager@redwood in 15m.

sara: thanks team. closing the live mitigation loop. We'll reconvene for the postmortem. :white_check_mark:
